def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Return the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Heap algorithm.
    The time complexity is O(n + k log n).
    """

    import heapq
    
    if k < 1 or k > len(nums):
        raise ValueError("k must be between 1 and the length of the list")

    # Create a min-heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)
    
    # Process the remaining elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:  # Only add to the heap if the number is larger than the smallest in the heap
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest element in the heap
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Add the new number to the heap

    return min_heap[0]  # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Return the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Heap-based approach.
    The time complexity is O(n log k) due to maintaining a heap of size k.
    """
    import heapq
    
    if k < 1 or k > len(nums):
        raise ValueError("k must be between 1 and the length of the list")
    
    # Create a min heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)
    
    # Process the remaining elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:  # Only push to heap if the current number is larger than the smallest in the heap
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Add the current number
    
    return min_heap[0]  # The top of the min heap is the k-th largest element
